description: Engineer and iterate prompts for an LLM application from task definition through benchmarking.

steps.description: Define the task, success criteria, and evaluation rubric for the prompt.

inputs.name: success-criteria
inputs.desc: Measurable criteria for a correct output

process: State the task in precise terms with input and output format.
List the success criteria with pass/fail thresholds.
Write the evaluation rubric with scoring dimensions.
Compile example inputs and their expected outputs.

steps.description: Write the initial prompt with few-shot examples and formatting instructions.
process: Write the system prompt with role and constraints.
Add few-shot examples that cover common cases.
Specify the output format and guardrails.
Document the rationale for each prompt section.

steps.description: Test the prompt against a sample set and score the outputs.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Scored results for each test case

outputs.name: failure-cases
outputs.desc: Cases that did not meet criteria

process: Run the prompt against each test input.
Score each output against the rubric.
Identify failure patterns and edge cases.
Calculate the overall pass rate.

steps.description: Revise the prompt to address failure cases and edge cases.
process: Analyze each failure to find the root cause.
Revise the prompt to handle each failure pattern.
Add or update examples to cover edge cases.
Document every change and its justification.

steps.description: Add output formatting, validation rules, and safety guardrails.

outputs.name: guardrail-spec
outputs.desc: List of all guardrails and their purposes

process: Define output format constraints (JSON schema, markdown, etc.).
Add safety guardrails for off-topic or harmful outputs.
Add validation rules for expected output structure.
Test that guardrails do not block valid outputs.

steps.description: Benchmark the final prompt against the baseline and produce the report.

outputs.name: benchmark-report
outputs.desc: Comparison of final prompt vs baseline

process: Run the final prompt against the full evaluation set.
Compare metrics to the baseline results.
Document the improvement on each scoring dimension.
Package the prompt with its rationale, rubric, and benchmark data.

description: Fine-tune a language model from dataset preparation through deployment.

steps.description: Prepare and validate the training dataset for fine-tuning.

inputs.name: task-definition
inputs.desc: What the fine-tuned model must do

outputs.name: formatted-dataset
outputs.desc: Dataset in the required format (JSONL, chat format)

outputs.name: data-report
outputs.desc: Statistics on the dataset (size, distribution, quality)

process: Convert the data to the required format (instruction/response pairs or chat).
Clean duplicates, low-quality examples, and formatting errors.
Split into train, validation, and test sets.
Validate the format against the training platform requirements.

steps.description: Select the base model and fine-tuning method.

inputs.name: task-definition
inputs.desc: What the fine-tuned model must do

outputs.name: model-selection
outputs.desc: Selected base model and method (LoRA, QLoRA, full)

process: Evaluate candidate base models by capability and size.
Select the fine-tuning method based on dataset size and compute budget.
Estimate the GPU hours and memory requirements.
Document the selection rationale.

steps.description: Configure the training hyperparameters and environment.
process: Set the learning rate, batch size, and number of epochs.
Configure LoRA rank, alpha, and target modules if applicable.
Set early stopping criteria and checkpointing.
Document the full configuration for reproducibility.

steps.description: Execute the fine-tuning job and monitor progress.

outputs.name: training-log
outputs.desc: Loss curves, metrics, and training events

process: Launch the training job with the configuration.
Monitor loss curves for divergence or overfitting.
Save checkpoints at regular intervals.
Select the best checkpoint by validation loss.

steps.description: Evaluate the fine-tuned model on the held-out test set.
process: Run inference on the test set with the fine-tuned model.
Compute task-specific metrics (accuracy, F1, BLEU, etc.).
Compare against the base model baseline.
Document the improvements and remaining weaknesses.

steps.description: Deploy the fine-tuned model to an inference endpoint.

outputs.name: deployment-endpoint
outputs.desc: URL and configuration of the serving endpoint

outputs.name: deployment-runbook
outputs.desc: Operations runbook for the deployed model

process: Package the model for serving (quantize if needed).
Deploy to the inference platform.
Verify the endpoint returns correct outputs.
Write the operations runbook with monitoring and rollback steps.

description: Evaluate an AI system for safety across toxicity, bias, hallucination, jailbreak, and privacy categories.

steps.description: Define the safety categories and severity levels to evaluate.

inputs.name: system-description
inputs.desc: Description of the AI system under test

outputs.name: safety-taxonomy
outputs.desc: Categories with definitions and severity levels

outputs.name: evaluation-scope
outputs.desc: What is in and out of scope

process: List the safety categories relevant to the system.
Define severity levels for each category.
Specify what is in scope and out of scope.
Document the regulatory or policy requirements.

steps.description: Design test cases for each safety category.

outputs.name: adversarial-prompts
outputs.desc: Adversarial inputs designed to trigger failures

process: Write test cases for each category and severity level.
Design adversarial prompts for jailbreak and injection.
Include edge cases and ambiguous inputs.
Validate that test cases cover the full taxonomy.

steps.description: Execute the safety evaluation suite and collect results.
process: Run each test case against the system.
Record the system output and any safety violations.
Flag outputs that score below the threshold.
Log all failures with their category and severity.

steps.description: Score the results and identify failure patterns.

outputs.name: failure-analysis
outputs.desc: Patterns and root causes of failures

process: Score each output against the category thresholds.
Calculate pass rates by category.
Identify failure patterns across categories.
Rank failures by severity and frequency.

steps.description: Recommend mitigations for each identified failure.
process: Map each failure pattern to a mitigation strategy.
Prioritize mitigations by severity and feasibility.
Estimate the effort and risk for each mitigation.
Compile the full safety evaluation report.

description: Generate and validate synthetic data for model training or testing.

steps.description: Define the data schema, distributions, and constraints for synthetic generation.

inputs.name: real-data-sample
inputs.desc: Sample of the real data to replicate

inputs.name: generation-purpose
inputs.desc: Why synthetic data is needed (training, testing, privacy)

outputs.name: data-schema
outputs.desc: Schema with field types, ranges, and distributions

outputs.name: constraint-spec
outputs.desc: Constraints between fields and business rules

process: Profile the real data to extract schema and distributions.
Document the constraints between fields.
Identify sensitive fields that must not leak.
Define the target dataset size and format.

steps.description: Select the generation method based on the data type and purpose.

outputs.name: method-config
outputs.desc: Configuration parameters for the selected method

process: Evaluate candidate methods against the data type.
Assess privacy guarantees of each method.
Select the method that balances fidelity and privacy.
Configure the generation parameters.

steps.description: Generate the synthetic dataset using the selected method.
process: Run the generation process with the configuration.
Apply all constraints and business rules.
Validate the output schema matches the specification.
Log the generation parameters for reproducibility.

steps.description: Validate the synthetic data against the real data distributions.

outputs.name: fidelity-report
outputs.desc: Statistical comparison of synthetic vs real

process: Compare marginal distributions between synthetic and real.
Check correlations and joint distributions.
Run privacy leakage tests (membership inference, attribute inference).
Report fidelity scores and privacy risk levels.

steps.description: Package the synthetic data with documentation for downstream use.

outputs.name: data-package
outputs.desc: Synthetic data with metadata and documentation

outputs.name: usage-guidelines
outputs.desc: Guidelines for using the synthetic data

process: Format the dataset for the target consumption platform.
Write the data card with schema, lineage, and limitations.
Document the approved use cases and restrictions.
Package with the fidelity report and generation log.

description: Set up a data annotation pipeline from schema definition through quality control.

steps.description: Define the annotation schema and labeling guidelines.

inputs.name: task-requirements
inputs.desc: What the annotations will be used for

outputs.name: annotation-schema
outputs.desc: Label taxonomy with definitions and examples

process: Define the label taxonomy with clear boundaries.
Write the annotation guidelines with positive and negative examples.
Handle ambiguous cases with decision rules.
Pilot the guidelines on a small sample to check clarity.

steps.description: Select and configure the annotation tool for the project.

inputs.name: data-samples
inputs.desc: Sample data to configure the tool

outputs.name: tool-documentation
outputs.desc: How to use the tool for this project

process: Select the annotation tool based on data type and schema.
Configure the label set and input format.
Set up the review and adjudication workflow.
Test the configuration with sample data.

steps.description: Train the annotation team on the schema and tools.

outputs.name: training-record
outputs.desc: Who was trained and their qualification scores

outputs.name: calibration-set
outputs.desc: Gold standard examples for ongoing calibration

process: Walk annotators through the guidelines and examples.
Run a qualification test on the calibration set.
Review errors and clarify edge cases.
Certify annotators who meet the quality threshold.

steps.description: Set up quality control with inter-annotator agreement and gold checks.

outputs.name: agreement-metrics
outputs.desc: Inter-annotator agreement baseline (Cohen kappa, Fleiss kappa)

process: Define the overlap rate for double annotation.
Set the inter-annotator agreement threshold.
Insert gold standard items at regular intervals.
Define the adjudication process for disagreements.

steps.description: Run the annotation batches and track progress.
process: Assign batches to annotators based on capacity.
Monitor quality metrics during annotation.
Flag and retrain annotators below the quality threshold.
Compile the final annotated dataset with quality report.

description: Build a model evaluation framework with automated and human evaluation protocols.

steps.description: Define the evaluation metrics for the task.

outputs.name: metric-set
outputs.desc: Selected metrics with definitions and thresholds

process: Identify the automatic metrics for the task type.
Define human evaluation dimensions (fluency, relevance, correctness).
Set the threshold for each metric.
Document how each metric is computed.

steps.description: Build the evaluation dataset with representative and adversarial examples.
process: Sample representative examples from production data.
Add adversarial and edge-case examples.
Create gold-standard labels for each example.
Validate coverage across important subgroups.

steps.description: Implement automated evaluation pipelines.
process: Implement each automatic metric as a scorer.
Build the evaluation pipeline to run all scorers.
Run the pipeline on the evaluation dataset.
Store baseline results for comparison.

steps.description: Design the human evaluation protocol.

outputs.name: human-eval-protocol
outputs.desc: Instructions, rubric, and workflow for human evaluators

process: Write the evaluation rubric for each human dimension.
Design the evaluation interface and workflow.
Define the number of evaluators per example.
Set the inter-rater agreement requirements.

steps.description: Package the evaluation framework with documentation.

outputs.name: framework-report
outputs.desc: Documentation of all metrics, datasets, and protocols

process: Combine automated and human evaluation into one framework.
Write the usage documentation.
Define the evaluation cadence and triggers.
Package for integration with the CI/CD pipeline.

description: Design a retrieval-augmented generation system from corpus selection through quality evaluation.

steps.description: Select and prepare the document corpus for retrieval.

inputs.name: use-case
inputs.desc: What questions the RAG system must answer

outputs.name: corpus-metadata
outputs.desc: Statistics on corpus size, types, and coverage

process: Inventory the available document sources.
Select documents relevant to the use case.
Clean and normalize the document formats.
Catalog the corpus with metadata.

steps.description: Choose and implement the chunking strategy.

outputs.name: chunking-config
outputs.desc: Strategy, size, overlap, and metadata settings

process: Evaluate chunking strategies (fixed-size, semantic, recursive).
Select chunk size and overlap based on the query type.
Preserve document structure and metadata in chunks.
Test that chunks contain enough context to answer queries.

steps.description: Select the embedding model and vector store, then index the chunks.

outputs.name: index-config
outputs.desc: Embedding model, dimensions, and index parameters

process: Evaluate embedding models by task and language.
Select the vector store and configure the index.
Embed and load all chunks.
Verify index health and query latency.

steps.description: Build the retrieval pipeline with query processing and reranking.
process: Implement query preprocessing (expansion, rewriting).
Configure top-k retrieval and similarity threshold.
Add reranking if precision matters more than latency.
Set metadata filters for scoped queries.

steps.description: Design the generation prompt that uses retrieved context.

outputs.name: prompt-guardrails
outputs.desc: Rules for hallucination prevention and citation

process: Write the system prompt with grounding instructions.
Design the context injection format.
Add citation requirements and hallucination guardrails.
Test with sample queries and retrieved contexts.

steps.description: Evaluate retrieval and generation quality end to end.
process: Evaluate retrieval quality (recall@k, MRR, precision@k).
Evaluate generation quality (faithfulness, relevance, completeness).
Test for hallucination on questions with no relevant context.
Compile the full design document with architecture and metrics.

description: Set up ML experiment tracking from platform selection through dashboard creation.

steps.description: Select the experiment tracking platform based on team needs.

inputs.name: team-requirements
inputs.desc: Team size, workflow, and integration needs

outputs.name: integration-plan
outputs.desc: How the platform fits the existing stack

process: Evaluate candidate platforms (MLflow, W&B, Neptune, ClearML).
Score by features, integrations, cost, and team fit.
Select the platform and document the rationale.
Plan the integration with existing infrastructure.

steps.description: Define naming conventions and metadata standards for experiments.

outputs.name: naming-conventions
outputs.desc: Standards for experiment, run, and artifact names

outputs.name: metadata-schema
outputs.desc: Required tags and metadata for every run

process: Define the experiment naming hierarchy (project, experiment, run).
Set the required metadata tags for every run.
Define the artifact naming and versioning scheme.
Document the conventions for the team.

steps.description: Configure metric, parameter, and artifact logging.

outputs.name: artifact-policy
outputs.desc: What artifacts to log and retention rules

process: Configure automatic metric logging.
Set up parameter logging for reproducibility.
Define which artifacts to save (models, datasets, plots).
Set retention and cleanup policies.

steps.description: Set up model versioning and the promotion workflow.

outputs.name: versioning-workflow
outputs.desc: Model versioning and stage promotion process

process: Configure the model registry.
Define the stage labels (development, staging, production).
Set the promotion criteria for each stage.
Document the approval workflow for production promotion.

steps.description: Build dashboards for comparing experiments and tracking progress.
process: Design the experiment comparison dashboard.
Add model registry status views.
Create team progress and cost tracking panels.
Document the full setup for onboarding new team members.

description: Build an AI governance framework from system inventory through periodic review.

steps.description: Inventory all AI systems in use across the organization.

inputs.name: inventory-criteria
inputs.desc: What qualifies as an AI system

outputs.name: ai-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all AI systems with purpose and owner

outputs.name: inventory-gaps
outputs.desc: Systems that could not be fully documented

process: Survey each department for AI system usage.
Document purpose, data inputs, outputs, and owner for each.
Identify systems that lack documentation.
Catalog third-party AI services and APIs.

steps.description: Classify each AI system by risk level.

outputs.name: risk-classification
outputs.desc: Each system assigned a risk tier

process: Define risk tiers (minimal, limited, high, unacceptable).
Assess each system against the criteria (impact, autonomy, data sensitivity).
Assign a risk tier to each system.
Document the rationale for each classification.

steps.description: Define approval gates and controls for each risk tier.

outputs.name: approval-gates
outputs.desc: Required approvals and reviews per risk tier

outputs.name: control-requirements
outputs.desc: Technical and process controls per tier

process: Define the approval process for each risk tier.
Set the technical controls (monitoring, logging, access).
Assign review responsibilities.
Document the gate criteria for passing.

steps.description: Set monitoring and alerting requirements for AI systems.

outputs.name: monitoring-requirements
outputs.desc: What to monitor per system and how

process: Define the monitoring metrics per system type.
Set alerting thresholds for drift, bias, and errors.
Define the escalation path for each alert type.
Document the monitoring cadence and reporting.

steps.description: Establish an incident response protocol for AI failures.

outputs.name: ai-incident-protocol
outputs.desc: Incident response procedures for AI failures

outputs.name: escalation-matrix
outputs.desc: Who to contact for each system and failure type

process: Define AI-specific incident categories.
Write the response playbook for each category.
Build the escalation matrix.
Schedule tabletop exercises to test the protocol.

steps.description: Schedule periodic reviews and produce the governance framework document.
process: Set the review cadence per risk tier.
Define what each review must cover.
Assign review owners.
Compile the full governance framework document.

description: Set up a vector database from use-case definition through performance benchmarking.

steps.description: Analyze the use case and define query patterns for the vector database.

inputs.name: use-case
inputs.desc: What the vector database will be used for

inputs.name: data-profile
inputs.desc: Description of the data to store

outputs.name: query-patterns
outputs.desc: Expected query types, volumes, and latency needs

process: Document the primary query patterns.
Estimate query volume and latency requirements.
Define the data size and growth projections.
List the filtering and metadata needs.

steps.description: Evaluate and select the vector database platform.
process: Evaluate candidates (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector, Milvus).
Score each against the requirements.
Consider operational complexity and cost.
Document the selection rationale.

steps.description: Design the index configuration for the selected platform.
process: Set the vector dimensions and distance metric.
Configure the index algorithm parameters (HNSW M, efConstruction).
Design the metadata schema for filtering.
Set the replication and sharding configuration.

steps.description: Load vectors into the database and verify integrity.
process: Batch the vectors for efficient loading.
Load with progress tracking and error handling.
Verify the count matches the source.
Spot-check retrieval on known vectors.

steps.description: Benchmark query performance and produce the setup document.
process: Run latency benchmarks at target query volume.
Measure recall against a ground truth set.
Test under concurrent load.
Compile the full setup document with architecture and metrics.

description: Audit and optimize LLM inference costs across an organization.

steps.description: Audit current LLM usage by model, endpoint, and cost.

inputs.name: billing-data
inputs.desc: LLM API billing and usage records

outputs.name: usage-breakdown
outputs.desc: Usage by model, application, and cost center

process: Collect billing data by model and endpoint.
Map usage to applications and teams.
Identify the top cost drivers.
Calculate the cost per query for each application.

steps.description: Identify caching opportunities for repeated or similar queries.

outputs.name: cache-opportunities
outputs.desc: Queries suitable for semantic or exact caching

process: Analyze query logs for exact duplicates.
Identify semantically similar queries that return the same answer.
Estimate the cache hit rate for each application.
Project the cost savings from each caching strategy.

steps.description: Reduce token usage through prompt compression and optimization.

outputs.name: compression-report
outputs.desc: Token reduction per prompt and quality impact

process: Identify prompts with the highest token counts.
Remove redundant instructions and examples.
Compress system prompts without losing quality.
Measure the quality impact of each compression.

steps.description: Evaluate smaller or cheaper models for qualifying use cases.

outputs.name: model-recommendations
outputs.desc: Cheaper model alternatives per use case

outputs.name: quality-comparison
outputs.desc: Quality vs cost tradeoff for each switch

process: Identify use cases that do not need the largest model.
Test smaller models on each qualifying use case.
Compare quality and cost for each alternative.
Recommend the model for each use case.

steps.description: Set up ongoing cost tracking and produce the optimization report.

outputs.name: optimization-report
outputs.desc: Full cost optimization report with action items

process: Set up cost-per-query tracking by application.
Configure budget alerts and anomaly detection.
Create the cost dashboard.
Compile the optimization report with projected savings.

description: Respond to an AI system incident from detection through post-incident review.

steps.description: Detect and classify the AI system incident.

outputs.name: incident-classification
outputs.desc: Type (hallucination, bias, safety, performance) and severity

outputs.name: impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Scope and affected users or systems

process: Confirm the incident is real (not a false positive).
Classify the incident type and severity.
Assess the scope (how many users, transactions, or decisions affected).
Notify the incident response team.

steps.description: Implement immediate mitigation to limit harm.

outputs.name: system-state
outputs.desc: Current state after mitigation (rolled back, traffic rerouted, etc.)

process: Decide the mitigation action (rollback, traffic reroute, feature disable).
Execute the mitigation.
Verify that the mitigation stopped the harm.
Communicate the status to stakeholders.

steps.description: Investigate the root cause of the incident.
process: Collect logs, model outputs, and input data from the incident window.
Reproduce the failure in a test environment.
Identify the root cause (data drift, prompt issue, model degradation, adversarial input).
Document the investigation timeline and evidence.

steps.description: Deploy the fix and verify resolution.
process: Develop the fix (retrain, prompt update, guardrail addition).
Test the fix against the original failure cases.
Deploy the fix and remove temporary mitigations.
Add monitoring to detect recurrence.

steps.description: Conduct the post-incident review and produce the report.

outputs.name: post-incident-report
outputs.desc: Full incident report with timeline, root cause, and actions

process: Write the incident timeline from detection to resolution.
Document the root cause and contributing factors.
List the action items for systemic improvement.
Schedule the follow-up review to verify actions completed.
